chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he
was asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

key_terms.أَيُؤْكَلُ مِنْهُ: May one eat from it — the jurisprudential question about permissibility of consuming such game
key_terms.الْبُنْدُقُ: The pellet/bullet — a small rounded projectile; in classical usage refers to a clay ball or rounded shot used in hunting; kills by blunt force
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The stone — a blunt projectile used in hunting; kills by impact rather than cutting
key_terms.قَتَلَ: Kills — used here for game killed by impact (not by lawful slaughter)

ai.seo_question: Is an animal killed by a stone or pellet permissible to eat in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked whether animals killed by a stone or pellet (a projectile that kills by blunt force rather than cutting) are permissible to eat. He ruled categorically that they are not permissible. In Islamic jurisprudence, lawful slaughter (dhabh) requires cutting the throat with a sharp implement to allow blood to drain; an animal killed by blunt-force impact does not fulfill this condition and is therefore forbidden (haram) to consume.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having been asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet, can one eat from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once, abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
was asked about a prey killed by stone or clay-ball; if it is edible. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it cannot be used for food. 5 ”
